# Kolkrabbi

> Kolkrabbi (binary: kolk) is an open-source, model-agnostic AI coding agent for the terminal —
> an alternative to Claude Code and Codex CLI. Apache-2.0, macOS and Linux. Written in Go: one
> static binary under 9 MB, milliseconds to start, two dependencies.

Install: curl -fsSL https://kolkrabbi.francomichetti.com/install.sh | sh
Or: brew install onembyte/tap/kolk  (macOS and Linux; `kolkrabbi` is an alias for `kolk`,
     usable as a short name after `brew trust onembyte/tap`)
Source: https://github.com/onembyte/kolkrabbi

## Providers that work today

- OpenRouter — every model it lists. The gateway: GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen and the rest
  arrive this way.
- Anthropic — Claude Free, Pro and Max, through your own installed `claude` CLI.
- OpenAI — ChatGPT Plus and Pro, through your own installed Codex CLI.
- Ollama — local models, found automatically. kolk never installs one.
- vLLM — self-hosted, over an OpenAI-compatible URL.
- LiteLLM — any proxy over an OpenAI-compatible URL.

kolk never sees, stores or refreshes a subscription credential. The vendor's own CLI performs the
login; kolk drives that CLI as a subprocess and records what comes back.

Google, xAI, Perplexity, Mistral, DeepSeek, Qwen, Cohere and GitHub Copilot have no direct
adapter yet. Most of those models are already reachable through the OpenRouter gateway.

## What makes it different

- One effort dial — low, medium, high, max — selects *which model* runs the turn and how wide the
  agent work goes, rather than only how many thinking tokens are spent.
- Three modes: chat (no tools), code (the read/write/edit loop), agent (work planned as
  dependency-ordered tasks, each routed to a model slot).
- Checkpoints are taken before every write, with /diff, /changes, /rewind and /undo.
- Every model call is appended to a local JSONL file you own. `/stats` inside the session shows
  calls, tokens, cost, latency and your own 1–5 ratings per model, so you can see which models
  earn their price. `/dash` opens the same numbers as a loopback-only page.
- No telemetry, no analytics, no cloud sync, no background version check.
- Starts free: given no model, it picks a zero-cost, tool-capable model from OpenRouter's live
  catalog.
- Releases are signed with keyless Cosign, and the install script verifies SHA-256 against the
  release checksums before installing anything.

## What it does not have yet

- No MCP, no skills, no general execution sandbox, no LSP.
- Starting a session still expects a gateway (OpenRouter) key, even when a Claude or
  ChatGPT subscription is what answers the turns.
- Windows is cross-built in CI but not supported. macOS and Linux are.
- Changes made by the `bash` tool are not checkpointed.
- Subagents share one working tree; there is no worktree isolation.
- Markdown slash commands and post-edit, post-write and session-end hooks do exist.

## Guides
- Local models — Ollama, vLLM, LiteLLM, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint:
  https://kolkrabbi.francomichetti.com/local-ai-coding-agent
- Ollama, step by step: https://kolkrabbi.francomichetti.com/ollama-coding-agent
- OpenRouter, the free start and the effort dial:
  https://kolkrabbi.francomichetti.com/openrouter-coding-agent

## Benchmarks
- KolkBench, a pre-registered benchmark of harnesses rather than models. First result, 2026-09-05:
  on a local 8B model, Kolkrabbi, Codex CLI and OpenCode all scored 0 of 18 — including ours.
  https://kolkrabbi.francomichetti.com/benchmarks
